Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20, read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

Records analysed: 759 (2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time window)
Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED probability (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — the LBNL catalogue magnitudes are calibrated, so this is the calibrated estimate):
  b=1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(Mw>=5.5) in observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
  b=0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922,  P(Mw>=5.5) in observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
  b=0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474,   P(Mw>=5.5) in observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated catalogue-based probability of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is at most ~1.5e-2 per year (b=0.65 scenario), i.e. very low; the DAS-based figure (0.078/yr) is only an upper bound because the DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all 62 detections are counted as events above Mc, over-counting relative to the calibrated LBNL catalogue.
